newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Fuel oil weighed down by stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Fuel oil weighed down by stocks.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps extended its early day slide late Friday afternoon on market expectations that sellers would emerge to take on recent bids by a Singapore trader in the face of high stocks, traders said.
"There is enough oil around...and I think more sellers will come out this evening," one trader said.
April fuel oil swaps were last quoted $99.50/$100.50 per tonne, down from Thursday's $103.00/104.00 per tonne, brokers said.
Trading was thin as sellers were not keen to sell at the lower levels when compared to Thursday's traded level of $102.00 per tonne and the $103.00 traded high chalked up late Wednesday.
In the physical market, a trader bought a 20,000-tonne cargo late Thursday at $104.00 per tonne loading April 15-19 free-on-board Singapore, compared to $99.00 traded on Tuesday.
Stock levels in Singapore are high despite the 932,000-barrels draw to 11.76 million barrels for the week ending March 19 as in the previous week there was a 2.097 million barrel build.
On top of this, an expected 200,000-tonnes of arbitrage cargoes are due to arrive in April.
The gas oil market firmed on expectations of a fairly high Indian Oil Corp award in line with the past two months with strong prompt support still likely from a Singapore trader.
The April gas oil was last quoted firmer at $26.60/$26.70, from Thursday's $26.30/$26.50, brokers said. It traded this morning at $26.50.
The April/May time spread remains wide and was traded earlier in the day at 85 cents.
The April jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) was actively traded at around the 30 cents mark on fears that the gas oil market would come under strong downward correction in April.
Brokers said April regrade traded at 30 cents, 35 cents and 32 cents earlier in the day.
